title: Polaris Telehealth VPC Compatibility Runbook (WIP)
content:
Status: WIP - working runbook for Polaris Telehealth private deployment

Overview
- Customer: Polaris Telehealth (HIPAA-sensitive telemedicine workflows).
- Purpose: Capture compatibility checks, sizing assumptions, Terraform module notes, and an upgrade/rollback plan for a VPC-hosted Private deployment (single-region, active-app with DR standby).
- Owner: Ava Thompson (eng-private-deployments).
- Context: Polaris wants a private deployment inside their GCP project with KMS-integration and a controlled upgrade window (2 hours) during low clinical traffic (02:00–04:00 local).

Executive summary / key constraints
- Hard latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for text-gen single-turn requests (seq len 512).
- Dedicate a minimum of 2x A100-80GB equivalents for inference layer initially; target 4x for steady-state.
- Storage: model artifacts pulled from our artifact registry via signed URLs; customer requires model artifacts to be stored in their GCS bucket (private).
- Network: Private service connect + VPC-SC approved; no public ingress to inference nodes.
- Compliance: Must integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping. Audit logs required for all calls to the model serving control plane.

Sizing assumptions (initial proposal)
- Workload profile (observed from pilot): 120 reqs/min peak, average seq=320 tokens, ~45% cache-hit expected after prefix warmups.
- Token throughput estimate (Rough): 120 reqs/min * 320 tokens = 38,400 tokens/min => ~640 tokens/sec.
- GPU baseline: 2 A100-80GB gives ~300–400 tokens/sec for mixed batch sizes; 4 nodes recommended for headroom and autoscaling buffer.
- CPU/Memory per host: 32 vCPU, 256GB RAM for control/relay node; CUDA hosts match GPU machine types.
- Disk: 1TB NVMe local cache per inference host for models + KV cache.

Terraform & infra notes (module boundaries)
- Module layout suggestion (to be reflected in polaris-deploy repo):
  - modules/network: VPC, subnets, firewall rules, private-service-connect endpoints.
  - modules/kms-integration: IAM bindings, KMS key grants scoped to Redwood service account principals.
  - modules/storage: GCS bucket ACLs, signed URL role bindings, artifact access service account.
  - modules/compute: instance templates, managed instance groups for inference, startup scripts to mount artifact registry.
  - modules/ops: Cloud Logging sinks, error reporting, monitoring alerting policies.
- State handling: Use customer-managed GCS backend for Terraform state (they prefer not to give us state buckets). Use remote state in a customer-owned bucket with restricted ACLs. Document workflows for state-locking (use Cloud Storage-based locking via Terraform).
- Sensitive variables: KMS key ring ID, service account emails MUST NOT be in plain tfvars in repo. Use HashiCorp Vault or Terraform Cloud with workspace variables.

Module operational notes and gotchas (lessons from prior customers)
- Private service connect: DNS split-horizon plus PSC requires careful order of creation; create forwarding rules after endpoints or traffic to PSC will fail.
- IAM: Least-privilege is OK but service account must be pre-provisioned with Storage Object Viewer on customer model bucket. Customer often forgets to add the SA to KMS key members. Check early.
- GKE vs. VM pool: For this customer we recommend VM pool (managed instance group) to avoid GKE node auto-updates during clinical hours. If they insist on GKE, pin node pool release channels.
- Model load vs. startup time: large quantized model pulls can take 6–12 minutes on first pull; pre-warm images during maintenance window.

Upgrade plan (minor version / runtime patch)
- Objectives: 0–2% request error budget increase during 2-hour window; fast rollback to previous AMI/container tag within 20 minutes if regression.
- Phased rollout steps:
  1) Validation: deploy new AMI/container to shadow MG (size=1) in staging within customer VPC (dry-run network only). Smoke tests: model-load, sample-gen, KV cache hit curve.
  2) Canary: deploy to 1 inference host in prod pool (5% traffic via routing rule). Monitor p95 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization for 30 minutes.
  3) Incremental: double canary capacity every 20 minutes while observing metrics until 50% cutover.
  4) Full ramp: autoscale to target capacity; continue to monitor for 30 minutes before closing the window.
- Rollback triggers:
  - p95 latency > 250ms sustained 5m
  - error rate > 1% absolute or spike > 3x baseline
  - model quality regression detected by eval harness (if integrated)
- Rollback procedure:
  - Re-route traffic away from updated hosts back to previous host group via routing policies (control-plane API call). If policy cannot route, revert instance template to previous image and trigger rolling restart (expect ~12 min to reprovision per host).

Rollback playbook (rapid)
- 00:00 Trigger: Alert page on-call SRE.
- 02:00 Assess: Confirm metrics in Console + run three sample generation checks.
- 05:00 Execute routing revert to stable model variant (control plane step) — expect near-immediate fallback for new requests.
- 12:00 If routing revert fails or persistent degradation -> trigger rolling restart of instance group to previous image and mark incident as SEV2.

Architecture Q&A (polaris-specific)
- Q: Can we use customer's KMS for token encryption and signing?
  A: Yes but we need KMS key grant to Redwood SA. Document service account email and minimal IAM role (roles/cloudkms.cryptoOperator or custom limited role).
- Q: Can inference nodes access internet for OS package updates?
  A: Polaris disallows direct egress. Solution: use private NAT with URL allowlist for artifact registry domains. Pre-bake critical packages into image.
- Q: Where will logs land?
  A: Cloud Logging into a customer-owned log bucket. Export subset to Redwood for support via dedicated sink with restricted filter.

Acceptance criteria (pre-launch)
- Smoke tests: model load < 10 min for warm cache baseline, sample generation meets p95 <= 200ms on 95% of sample set.
- Security: KMS integration verified, audit logs present for control-plane actions.
- Terraform: Apply + destroy executed in customer dev project without manual drift fixes. State locked in customer GCS bucket and documented.
- Observability: Alerts created in prod project; alert routing to Polaris SRE + Redwood on-call.

Open questions / action items
- [ ] Polaris to provide KMS key ARN + confirm service account principal (INF-4132). Owner: Priya. Due: 2025-01-20.
- [ ] Decide whether to use customer-managed GKE node pools or VM MIGs. Owner: Diego. Due: 2025-01-22.
- [ ] Confirm maintenance window and blackout dates (Polaris clinical calendar). Owner: Ava. Due: 2025-01-18.
- [ ] Security review for private-service-connect plan; schedule review with customer security team. Owner: Liam. Due: 2025-01-25.

Notes to self / rough checklist (internal)
- Write Terraform docs for modules/network and modules/kms-integration (minimal examples).
- Add example IAM policy snippets to repo (avoid embedding customer ids).
- Prep container AMI with baked quantized model example and smoke test harness.

Appendix: quick commands and snippets
- Example IAM grant (customer GCP):
  gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/PROJECT/locations/global/keyRings/kr --key my-key \
    --member=serviceAccount:polaris-redwood-sa@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter

- Terraform remote state example snippet (customer-owned GCS bucket):
  terraform {
    backend "gcs" {
      bucket = "polaris-tfstate-prod"
      prefix = "redwood/private-deploy"
    }
  }

-- end of runbook draft --

(Inline references: INF-4132, pol-deploy PR#88, Polaris security contact: security@polarishealth.example.com)
